## Home use or venue use

A home kegerator pours a few glasses at a time and sits in a games room or garage. A venue unit pours all night, so it needs stronger cooling, a robust tower and easy cleaning. If you plan to serve guests regularly at home, think of it as a small venue and choose accordingly. Our [venue guides](/venues/home-bars-man-caves/) show typical home bar setups.

## Cleaning and maintenance

Beer lines should be cleaned on a regular schedule with a line cleaner, and the tap and coupler rinsed. Clean the cabinet interior, check the door seals and keep the condenser free of dust. A kegerator that is looked after pours cleaner beer and lasts longer. Cleaning supplies are listed in our [covers and cleaning](/accessories-parts/covers-cleaning/) category.

## What affects the price

The cost of a kegerator depends on size, cooling capacity, the number of taps and the build quality. Commercial units cost more than compact domestic ones. Compare what is included, because a lower price can leave out the regulator or the cylinder. Look at the total cost of the full setup rather than the cabinet alone, and ask for a delivered price through the [quote form](/quote/) if you are buying more than one.

## Compressor or thermoelectric cooling

Compressor wine fridges cool strongly and cope with warm rooms, which suits most Australian homes in summer. Thermoelectric models are quieter and produce almost no vibration, but they cool less powerfully and work best in cooler rooms. If your wine fridge will sit in a kitchen that gets warm, compressor cooling is usually the safer choice. Check the climate class in the specification.

## Noise and energy use

A wine cooler runs all day, so noise and power use matter. Quiet operation matters in an open-plan living area, and energy information on the product page helps you compare. A well-insulated cabinet with good seals runs less often, which helps both noise and running cost.

## Where to put it

Keep the cabinet away from direct sun, ovens and dishwashers. Choose a level spot and leave the clearance gaps in the manual. If the fridge sits near a window, a solid or UV-protective door helps shield the bottles. For a bar, see our [bar fridges](/bar-fridges/) and [glass door bar fridge guide](/guides/glass-door-bar-fridge-buying-guide/) for display ideas.

## Care and cleaning

Wipe the interior regularly with a mild cleaner, avoid strong scents that can taint the cabinet and check the door seal. Leave a gap between bottles so air moves freely. Replace water or charcoal filters if your model has them, following the manual.

## Setting the two zones

A common approach is to keep the lower zone a little warmer for reds and the upper zone cooler for whites and sparkling. If you use the cabinet as a wine and beverage fridge, set one zone for drinks and one for wine. Follow the manual for the safe range of each zone, and allow time for the cabinet to settle after you change the setting.

## Who benefits most

- Entertainers who serve both red and white
- Households with a mixed collection of wine and other drinks
- Small venues that want a compact display

If you only store a few bottles for ageing, a single zone wine fridge is simpler and often cheaper. You can see the range in our [bar fridges](/bar-fridges/) section, and our [bar fridge size guide](/guides/bar-fridge-size-guide-90l-125l-and-larger/) helps you plan the space.

## Running cost and noise

Two zones can mean extra components, so compare the energy information on the product page. A quiet wine cooler suits an open-plan living area, and a well-sealed cabinet runs less often. Place it where air can circulate and away from direct sun.

## Questions to ask before you buy

- Are the two zones fully independent?
- What is the temperature range of each zone?
- How many bottles fit per zone?
- What is the warranty and who handles a claim?

Having the answers up front keeps the comparison honest between models.

## Organising a chest freezer

Without a plan, a chest freezer becomes a pile. Use baskets for small items, label the lids of containers and keep a list of what is inside. Put older stock on top and freeze food flat so it stacks and thaws faster. Leave a little space for air to move so the freezer can hold temperature.

## Running costs and noise

A freezer runs constantly, so energy information matters. Compare the stated energy use, and check noise levels for models placed in living areas. A full freezer holds cold better than an empty one, so avoid running a much larger unit than you need. If you are weighing an upright instead, our [commercial freezer guide](/guides/commercial-freezer-for-sale-upright-vs-chest/) lists the differences.

## Power cuts and safety

Keep the lid closed during a power cut and the contents stay frozen longer. Do not refreeze food that has fully thawed. For a venue, a commercial chest freezer with a lock and a temperature alarm gives extra protection for valuable stock.

## Delivery and installation

Measure the doorway, the path and the final spot. Let the freezer stand upright before switching it on if the manual recommends it, then give it time to reach temperature before loading. Check the unit for transit damage and report anything straight away. Our [delivery information](/delivery/) explains how orders reach you, and our [cheap bar fridge guide](/guides/cheap-bar-fridge-australia-what-to-check/) has budget checks that apply to freezers too.

## Temperature and food safety

Frozen food must stay at a safe temperature throughout service. Choose a unit with a clear temperature display and, ideally, an alarm. Check the temperature regularly and keep a log if your business requires one. Do not rely on a freezer in a hot, unventilated room to hold temperature.

## Choosing by venue type

- Bars and pubs: under bar and back bar freezers for ice and frozen food, see [bar freezers](/bar-freezers/)
- Cafes and restaurants: upright freezers for kitchen storage
- Ice cream and gelato shops: display freezers for front of house
- Catering businesses: chest freezers for bulk storage

Our [venue guides](/venues/pubs-hotels/) show typical equipment for each type of business.

## Maintenance and cleaning

Clean the condenser and the door seals regularly, defrost manual units on schedule and keep the area around the freezer clear. Replace worn seals promptly. Our [chest freezer guide](/guides/chest-freezer-for-sale-sizes-and-checks/) explains defrosting and care in more detail.

## Warranty and parts

Commercial freezers should come with a clear warranty and access to parts. Ask what is covered and how a claim works. Our [warranty page](/warranty/) explains how claims are handled.
